::: {#def-vanishing-gradient}

#### Vanishing gradient

A network has a **vanishing gradient** when the gradient of its loss with respect to the [parameters](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-parameter) of its early layers
is many orders of magnitude smaller than with respect to those of its later layers,
because [backpropagation](#def-backpropagation) multiplies it by a factor smaller than 1 at each layer
[@glorot2010understanding; @goodfellow2016deep, section 8.2.5].
The early layers then learn far more slowly than the later ones, or not at all.

The opposite, a gradient that grows layer by layer, is an [exploding gradient](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/backpropagation.html#def-exploding-gradient).

:::
